values: Use this to add a new article, or to correct one already loaded.
One row per material, per size range, per production stage. Required — without it an article cannot be planned.
One row per BOM size range or individual size: how many pairs fit in its carton. Required for carton orders.
One row per article and size range or individual size. MRP is optional. Write Small 7 as 7S; write Large 7 as 7 (7L is also accepted).
THE THREE THINGS PEOPLE GET WRONG
Rate per Pair is for ONE PAIR. Not per carton, not per dozen, not per hundred.
Repeat Article Code, Sole Type and Size Range on EVERY BOM row. In Packing/Catalogue, use a range such as 7X10 or an individual size such as 7S (Small) or 7 / 7L (Large).
Use one spelling per material. MESH 58" and Mesh-58" would be bought as two different materials, splitting the requirement between them.
EVA, PVC, PU, STUCK-ON   (dropdown on the BOM tab)

ROTARY or VERTICAL. Only for PVC articles — leave blank for any other sole.
Leave blank for factory defaults, use SELF for a separate chart, or enter an existing source article such as ARMOUR.

HOW S / L SIZES ARE READ
Write S or Small for the Small run and L or Large for the Large run. Accepted examples: 7S, S7, 7L, L7.
Keep the factory order: all Small sizes first, then all Large sizes. Factory OS shows a warning whenever it uses this fallback.
7, 8, 1, 2, 3 is read as Small 7, Small 8, then Large 1, 2, 3. After the Large run starts, later 7–13 are Large.

values: Preferred: write Small or Large when a range repeats. If blank, Factory OS follows the uploaded range order: all Small ranges first, then Large.
Size Range may be a combo or one size. Write S/L where available. For a standalone size, BOM Range tells Factory OS which BOM and carton context it uses.
Catalogue — details and optional MRP by range or size
Repeat the exact Article Code. Size entries accept 7S/7L (also S7/L7). BOM Range is only needed when an individual size must borrow a particular range.
